title: Lease-based garbage collection for prefix-fair eviction with bounded staleness guarantees
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Prefix-aware caching currently uses TTL+LRU heuristics that can cause unfair eviction across tenants and prefixes under bursty continuous batching. This leads to elevated miss rates for long-lived prefixes and occasional tail-latency spikes when GPU slabs are reclaimed mid-inflight.

Proposal: Introduce a lease-based garbage collector that ties KV entries to short-lived leases (lease windows) granted at placement time. Leases provide explicit liveness semantics to the eviction subsystem, enabling: 1) safe reclamation only after all in-flight batches referencing a lease have completed, 2) prefix-fair quota enforcement via per-prefix active-lease counters, 3) bounded-staleness guarantees by combining lease durations with an epoch heartbeat mechanism and optional TTL fallback.

This ticket scopes the design, a reference implementation in the runtime eviction layer, and the correctness invariants + tests required for rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes lease acquisition and release paths integrated with continuous batching path: batch start acquires relevant prefix leases; batch completion releases them.
Garbage collector will not free any KV entry with active lease references; verified via stress test that simulates 100k concurrent batches and adversarial eviction pressure.
Per-prefix fairness: when a tenant's prefix is pinned by active leases > configured quota, new allocations are throttled/backpressured and metrics reflect pinned bytes and throttled-allocs.

Bounded staleness: combination of lease_max_duration + epoch-confirmation ensures no entry reclaimed while a batch that saw the entry is still inflight; correctness tests demonstrate staleness <= lease_max_duration + epoch_skew.
No regression on throughput or p99 latency under normal workloads (<5% regression compared to baseline with KV-lease disabled).
Feature guarded behind config flag and can be toggled without cluster restart; rollout plan documented.
implementation_notes: Lease lifecycle: leases are lightweight 64-bit tokens with (prefix_id, epoch, expiry_ts). Acquired at batch-routing time for all prefix keys used by requests in the batch.

Leases are reference-counted in an atomic slab map co-located with the per-GPU KV directory. Release flow must run on the same GPU worker thread to avoid cross-thread races; use async completion callbacks from batching layer.

Garbage collector: runs per-GPU and scans eviction candidates by watermark. Candidate is eligible only if: (a) no active leases, (b) last_access_ts < eviction_cutoff OR TTL expired, and (c) not part of pinned prefix set.

Prefix fairness: maintain a lightweight per-prefix active_lease_count and per-prefix reserved_bytes; eviction scores are adjusted by active_lease_count to avoid evicting from prefixes that are actively used.

Backpressure: when freeable memory falls below low_watermark and prefix reserved_bytes consumed, emit backpressure to router (batch admission controller) to refuse or delay new batches for offending prefixes.

Epoch heartbeat: control plane writes monotonically increasing epoch numbers to a shared metadata store; each lease is stamped with epoch at acquisition. During GC, if epoch_skew detected, conservative retention is used until an epoch-confirm passes.
Instrumentation: new metrics: lease_acquired, lease_released, lease_hold_time_histogram, gc_skipped_due_to_lease, prefix_throttled_batches, pinned_bytes_by_prefix.
Config knobs: lease_max_duration_ms (default 5000ms), lease_grace_ms (default 50ms), per_prefix_quota_bytes (default 10% of node), enable_lease_gc (false by default).

Performance: avoid per-key atomic ops on hot paths — batch-acquire uses a deduplicated prefix set and bumps a single per-prefix counter; individual KV entries only store a compact lease bitmap when needed.
test_plan: Unit tests: lease token encoding/decoding, lease expiry math, per-prefix counter race tests using thread-fuzz harness.

Integration: runtime e2e test that runs continuous batching generator (variable sequence lengths) while synthetic eviction pressure is applied to force reclamation; assert no invalidated cache references in live inference paths.
Chaos: cluster test that kills worker threads mid-batch and ensures leases held still prevent GC in-flight; verify eventual cleanup once worker restarts or lease expires.
Fuzz: mutate epoch numbers and simulate control-plane heartbeat loss to validate conservative GC behavior.

Performance: benchmark baseline vs lease-gc under production-like mixes (chatty small-prefix vs long conversation prefixes) measuring p50/p95/p99 token latency and throughput; compare GPU memory churn.
Correctness regression: add litmus tests that assert linearizability properties for read-after-free scenarios; these tests must pass on PRs before merge.
update_log: 2026-02-25: Ticket created. Initial problem statement and proposed lease-based approach. (Aisha)
2026-02-28: Design review: raised questions about epoch heartbeat availability in private deployments; agreed to add conservative fallback (TTL-only) when heartbeat absent. (Design + Infra)

2026-03-03: Prototype implemented in eviction branch; basic lease bookkeeping + per-prefix counters added. Microbenchmarks show 2% p99 regression on small seq lengths; investigating optimizations. (Liam)
2026-03-05: Added backpressure path to router to avoid allocation storms when pinned_bytes exceed quota. Integration tests added. (Liam)
2026-03-06: Submitted PRs 1892 and 1897 for code + tests. Requesting review from runtime and infra. (Liam)
2026-03-06: Marked In Review. Preparing rollout plan with feature flag and canary on dedicated nodes. (Aisha)
<future>: Post-merge actions: rollout to dedicated, monitor lease_hold_time and gc_skipped_due_to_lease; tune lease_max_duration.
comments: Miguel Torres (Infra): We need a clear story for control-plane epoch propagation in air-gapped deployments. Suggest default epoch behavior derived from node-local monotonic counter with cross-checks during periodic reconciliation.
Priya Nair (Platform): Make sure per-prefix quotas are configurable per-tenant; exposing a global default is fine but must support overrides for enterprise customers.
Jonah Park (SRE): Add alert for gc_skipped_due_to_lease spiking—could indicate leak or stalled workers. Also track leaked_lease_count metric.

Liam Chen: Implementation note — to avoid extra heap allocations, lease tokens will be stored inline in the KV header when the entry is pinned; otherwise the header remains compact. We still need to validate binary compatibility for on-disk snapshots.
